classification.difficultyReason: The hardest parts require selecting successive triangles or inferring parallel lines from perpendiculars, then linking parallel-line, straight-angle and triangle-sum facts while giving reasons.

content.prompt: Find the size of the marked angle $\angle AVB$ in each diagram, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle AVB with horizontal VB and interior PQ, matching single parallel arrows and the marked angle at V. Ordinary source-blue strokes become black.
spec.mathematics: P lies on AV, Q lies on AB, PQ is parallel to VB, angle VAB is 55 degrees and angle PQA is 28 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and an unlabelled angle arc only.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle APQ&=180^\circ-55^\circ-28^\circ\\\angle APQ&=97^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle APQ$.
$$\angle AVB=97^\circ$$
Corresponding angles, $PQ\parallel VB$.

spec.description: Triangle AVB with P on AV, Q on VB, PQ parallel to AB and marked angle at V.
spec.mathematics: Angle VAB is 85 degrees and angle VQP is 70 degrees; PQ and AB carry matching single parallel arrows.

answer.worked:
$$\angle VPQ=85^\circ$$
Corresponding angles, $PQ\parallel AB$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-85^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle AVB&=25^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle VPQ$, with $V,P,A$ collinear and $V,Q,B$ collinear.

spec.description: AOQ triangle, O–Q–B straight, P on AO, PB crossing AQ at V; the upper obtuse AVB sector is marked. A curved leader associates 20 degrees with the narrow angle PBQ at B.
spec.mathematics: Angle OAQ is 32 degrees, angle AOQ is 55 degrees and angle PBQ is 20 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and the target arc are visible.

answer.short:
$107^\circ$

Use the exterior angle of $\triangle AOQ$, then the exterior angle of $\triangle VQB$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle VQB&=32^\circ+55^\circ\\\angle VQB&=87^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle AOQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=87^\circ+20^\circ\\\angle AVB&=107^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle VQB$.

spec.description: R–V–A and A–P–B are straight; RP crosses VB at Q. Curved leaders associate the two 24-degree givens with R and B. The target arc is between VA and VB.
spec.mathematics: Angle ARP is 24 degrees, angle APR is 70 degrees and angle ABV is 24 degrees.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle RAP&=180^\circ-24^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle RAP&=86^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle RAP$. Since $R,V,A$ and $A,P,B$ are collinear, $\angle VAB=86^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-86^\circ-24^\circ\\\angle AVB&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle AVB$.

spec.description: P–B–A straight, AV parallel to PQ with matching arrows; BV joins the two sides to form ABV. Target arc at V.
spec.mathematics: Angle BPQ is 76 degrees and angle PBV is 140 degrees.

answer.short:
$36^\circ$

Use co-interior angles and a straight angle before the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAV&=180^\circ-76^\circ\\\angle BAV&=104^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $AV\parallel PQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABV&=180^\circ-140^\circ\\\angle ABV&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Straight angle $\angle ABP$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-104^\circ-40^\circ\\\angle AVB&=36^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle ABV$.

spec.description: Triangle AVP with B–V–P straight, QB parallel to AP and a target exterior angle AVB. The 86-degree leader points into QBV at B.
spec.mathematics: Angle QBV is 86 degrees and angle VAP is 25 degrees.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle APV&=180^\circ-86^\circ\\\angle APV&=94^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $QB\parallel AP$, with $B,V,P$ collinear.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=94^\circ+25^\circ\\\angle AVB&=119^\circ\end{align*}$$
Exterior angle of $\triangle AVP$.

spec.description: P–A–B lie on the left vertical line. PQ is horizontal and QV vertical, with right-angle squares at P and Q. AV and BV meet at V; the narrow AVB angle is marked.
spec.mathematics: Angle QVA is 140 degrees and angle ABV is 32 degrees. Both perpendicular marks are retained; no parallel arrows are added.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and target arc shown.

answer.short:
$8^\circ$

The two right angles establish $AB\parallel QV$; use this to find the angle at A.
answer.worked:
$AB\parallel QV$ because both lines are perpendicular to $PQ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle PAV&=180^\circ-140^\circ\\\angle PAV&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $AP\parallel QV$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAV&=180^\circ-40^\circ\\\angle BAV&=140^\circ\end{align*}$$
Straight angle $\angle PAB$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-140^\circ-32^\circ\\\angle AVB&=8^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle ABV$.

spec.description: Adjacent triangles PQV and QVB, with P–V–A and R–Q–B straight. All four given angles and the target exterior AVB arc are retained. No parallel arrows are supplied or added.
spec.mathematics: Angle VPQ is 72 degrees, angle PVQ is 55 degrees, angle RQP is 72 degrees and angle QBV is 72 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred parallel relationship or calculated angle is printed.

answer.short:
$72^\circ$

Find the angles at Q in the two triangles, then use the straight angle at V.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQV&=180^\circ-72^\circ-55^\circ\\\angle PQV&=53^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle PQV$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle VQB&=180^\circ-72^\circ-53^\circ\\\angle VQB&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles in straight angle $\angle RQB$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle QVB&=180^\circ-55^\circ-72^\circ\\\angle QVB&=53^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angle sum of $\triangle QVB$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=180^\circ-55^\circ-53^\circ\\\angle AVB&=72^\circ\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles in straight angle $\angle PVA$.
